payload.mechanism:
The writer and the reader BOTH use raw wall clock, at two different instants, at minute granularity. No shared rounding rule can bridge them.

WRITER (tick-snapshot.md Step 4.7): FILE_TICK=$(date -u +%H:%M), raw, no rounding. Key = nominal tick + dispatcher drift. Runs mid-tick, after drain/pressure/cadence/collision/slot-claim.

READER (skill Step -1): probes its own clock at spawn+1..3min. Two copies, both live in the fleet:
  Copy A (cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md:58) "round to nearest 5-min slot" -> hits ONLY if the writer's raw minute lands in the same 5-min bucket.
  Copy B (step-0-cowork/SKILL.md:39) raw wall clock -> hits ONLY if reader-minute == writer-minute exactly (sub-60s spawn-to-probe, no rollover).

Both are structurally capped well under 100% AGAINST THIS WRITER. Neither is "the correct copy". The 3-of-6 observed hit rate is what this geometry predicts, not noise.
payload.decisive_evidence:
c256 (2026-08-25T12:08:48Z, slot=alert-commander-critical, tick=12:00Z) is the designed discriminating sample and it returned Copy B:

  "no fresh tick-snapshot (no cycle-snapshot-12:07.json exact-tick match; 12:05.json ignored per exact-match rule)"

Probed 12:07 = raw wall clock. Copy A predicted 12:05 -> HIT (12:05 and 12:07 floor to the SAME bucket). Copy A is FALSIFIED for this cycle.

PER-INVOCATION VARIANCE IS BACK ON. Same agent, same flow file, three consecutive cycles: c254 and c255 probed 08:05 against writer file 08:05 (mtime 08:05:08Z) -- their spawn stamp was 08:06:37Z, so a raw probe was impossible and they must have rounded. c256 did not round. The derivation is not stable per-agent-per-flow. My earlier retirement of this hypothesis on the c254/c255 agreement was wrong: those two agreeing is trivially expected (both sat in the 08:0x bucket), so that pair never had discriminating power.
payload.fix_design_change:
THE KEY DOES NOT NEED TO AGREE AT ALL. This supersedes the fix I routed at 49f2c37ac.

Decisive new fact: the reader ENUMERATED THE DIRECTORY, SAW cycle-snapshot-12:05.json, and REJECTED it citing an "exact-match rule". That rule appears in NEITHER copy -- grep for exact/nearest/newest returns it in neither file. The agent supplied it to fill a gap in prose that specifies a key but never says what to do with a near-miss.

12:05.json was written 12:05:59Z and probed ~12:07:xx -- roughly 1-2 minutes old, comfortably inside the <=7-minute freshness gate that BOTH copies already specify (cycle-bootstrap:64, step-0-cowork:42-43). It was a valid, fresh, correct snapshot. It was discarded on a self-invented string comparison.

SMALLER FIX: delete the key lookup. Select the NEWEST docs/data/cycle-snapshot-*.json whose mtime is within the 7-minute window already specced. The filename becomes an opaque uniquifier and the freshness gate -- which both copies already agree on -- becomes the whole contract.

What this AVOIDS versus the routed design:
  - no writer change needed (tick-snapshot.md Step 4.7 filename and .tick can stay raw)
  - no scheduled_utc Consumer Contract extension past its date-only "leading 10 characters" scope
  - no nominal-tick alignment between two files that run minutes apart
  - cycle-snapshot-latest.json and its never-firing promoter become redundant (12 consecutive cycle_snapshot_promoted:false)

STILL REQUIRED regardless of which design lands: both copies change in ONE commit (best by deleting Copy B's inline restatement so only its pointer to Copy A survives), and the stale "snapshot writer is a future task ... Step -1 will always miss" note in cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md gets deleted -- the writer has been live and producing 31 files/day for some time.
payload.measured_distribution:
Writer-key minute distribution, all 31 cycle-snapshot files on disk (excludes -latest):
  on a 5-min boundary: 14   off-boundary: 17
Minutes: 05 x7, 49 x3, 34 x3, 20 x3, 50 x2, 35 x2, 04 x2, 02 x2, 36/33/31/23/19/18/03 x1 each.

So a Copy-A (rounding) reader is capped at ~45% by the writer's own key distribution before its own probe timing is even considered. The :05 cluster (7 of 31) is why Copy A hits as often as it does -- dispatcher drift is usually ~4-5 min, which lands the writer on a boundary by coincidence, not by design. This is the coincidence a writer-only fix would TRADE AWAY, which is why writer-only was never net-positive.
